### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**6** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c151c4993ee3a4409aadb1568865e4036cc4b01f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5b90fe2c09d29b201ff0d4dc1b4f1771fd7992cd` — the merge of head `291adbd71cef38cb43655c59730076347d03d047` into base `c151c4993ee3a4409aadb1568865e4036cc4b01f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5b90fe2c09d29b201ff0d4dc1b4f1771fd7992cd && git checkout 5b90fe2c09d29b201ff0d4dc1b4f1771fd7992cd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c151c4993ee3a4409aadb1568865e4036cc4b01f 291adbd71cef38cb43655c59730076347d03d047 && git checkout -B drift-repro c151c4993ee3a4409aadb1568865e4036cc4b01f && git merge --no-ff 291adbd71cef38cb43655c59730076347d03d047

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c151c4993ee3a4409aadb1568865e4036cc4b01f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `291adbd71cef38cb43655c59730076347d03d047`
Local-runs: probe — the two lookaheads are regular expressions whose reading of about 70 body shapes cannot be settled by eye; one `node` script called `hookRefusalCodesThrownIn` and `hookRefusalReasonsThrownIn` from the base blob and the head blob of the one `hits` file (`git show` copies in scratch, no checkout, no build, no test or gate run)
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/hook-refusal-codes.ts + none

Inputs read: card #36670 (body, triage 7100098534, claim 7226585955, amendment 7226609991; no ruling and no earlier record on the thread), PR #38044 (body, 4-file list, net diff against `main` at `3e8edf78`), the dev report for this head (`open_questions` empty, `out_of_scope_findings` empty), the check-runs on this head, and PR #36666 with its record 7099600018 as the cited precedent. Remainder of the diff, the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`: `.changeset/36670-refusal-literal-close.md`, `packages/spec/src/data/hook-refusals.test.ts`, `packages/spec/src/ui/action-refusals.test.ts`. Code read outside the diff, not reviewed: `packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts` (`refusalSourceOf`, `refuseUndeclaredLiteralRefusalCode`), `packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts` (`refuseUndeclaredLiteralActionRefusalCode`), `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/hook-refusal-catalogue.ts`, `content/docs/references/data/hook.mdx`.

Check-runs on this head, read 2026-11-27T20:21Z. Concluded success: `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, the three `Lint · scoped` runs, `PR-body guards`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build UI Deps`, `Check PR Size`, both shard plans. None failed. STILL PENDING at that read, so not yet a gate verdict: `Build Core`, `Test Core` 1 to 10 of 10, `Test UI` 1 to 16 of 16, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`. This verdict is on the contract; it does not stand in for those runs.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set, save doors of `HookSchema` and `ActionSchema` (the only callers, `hook.zod.ts:322,326` and `action.zod.ts:2781,2785`): WIDER by the bodies where a quoted code or reason is followed by something other than its form's terminator. Right for the class the card names: `code: 'OVER' + suffix`, `e.code = 'OVER' + suffix`, the reason twins, `.concat(...)` on the same or the next line, a blank or comment line before the continuation. Each read as the bare literal on `main` and is read as nothing on the head (probe).
- Refusal set kept for every ordinary literal: property closed by `}` or `,`, inside `Object.assign(new Error(), { ... })`, with a block or line comment before the close, CRLF, spread before or after, minified `{code:"X"}`; assignment closed by `;`, `,`, `}`, `)`, a line end (LF or CRLF), a trailing line comment, a block comment holding a line break, the source end, a comment line then a statement; a reason in `reasons: [ ... ]` and in `e.reasons = [ ... ]` (each item closes with `}` or `,`, a trailing comma included). Same path, same sentence: no `...AtSave` function moved. Right.
- Refusal set NOT kept for three valid-JavaScript literal shapes: see N1. The run-time refusal answers each.
- Second-order, not named by the PR: a code that becomes computed also moves the reason pairing. `throw { code: 'B', reason: 'r', cause: { code: 'A' + x } }` named two codes on `main` (so its reason was not read) and names one on the head, so `B.r` is now judged; `e.code = 'B'; e.code = 'A' + x; e.reason = 'r'` paired `r` with `A` on `main` and pairs it with `B` on the head. A body of either shape that saved on `main` (only possible with the never-thrown prefix `A` declared) can be refused on the head. This is the published pairing rule applied to a code now classified as the docblock classifies it; see N2.
- Run-time half unchanged and real: `hook-refusal-catalogue.ts` answers any thrown code the catalogue does not declare, and any undeclared reason under a code that declares `reasons`, through `undeclaredHookRefusalAtRun`, `undeclaredHookRefusalReasonAtRun` and the action twins, naming the code or reason. Every body the head newly accepts at save is still refused at run when the built value is undeclared. Right.
- Public surface: no export added, removed or retyped; both lookaheads and the four readers are module-private; no schema shape, `.describe()` or error sentence moved. Published prose elsewhere stays true unedited (`hook.mdx`: "at save when the hook throws it literally, otherwise at run time"; `hooks.mdx:452`). Right.
- Bodies are JavaScript at both doors: a `js` body is `z.literal('js')` source, and an inline handler is read through `Function.prototype.toString`, after type erasure. So `code: 'X' as const }` and `e.code = 'X' as Code;` (both dark on the head, probe) are not a loss: a syntax error in a `js` body, erased before a handler is read. Same finding as record 7099600018.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `Metadata-protocol: none`: right, as #36666 was ruled. A bug fix in a released package; no key, accepted value or metadata type is added, removed or re-meant. `Check Changeset` concluded success.
- Clause-②: no — holds. The save does accept bodies `main` refused, so the question is whether published text promised that refusal. It promised the opposite: the `hookRefusalCodesThrownIn` docblock on `main` ("A code that arrives any other way ... a computed value — is left to the run-time refusal"), the `hookRefusalReasonsThrownIn` docblock ("a computed reason"), the `hook.zod.ts` block ("A code that arrives any other way is the run-time refusal's") and the `refusals` `.describe()`. `'OVER' + suffix` is a computed value under each. The ground is the one record 7099600018 accepted for `hookTextKeysAskedIn`, and it carries over unchanged. No `(widening)` arm is owed. The N2 pairing effect does not earn `(narrowing)`: the published rule ("exactly one code literally"; "that name's literal `e.code = 'X'`") already says what the head does, and the bodies it reaches could only save on `main` by declaring a code they never throw.
- PR body and changeset carry the same two declaration lines.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. `out_of_scope_findings`: empty.
- Declared deviation 1, `,` added to the assignment terminators beyond the card's list: correct JavaScript. After a complete assignment value a comma is the comma operator or an argument or element separator, never part of the value, and `e.code = 'X', e.reason = 'r'` is the shape a minifier emits; leaving it out would have lost a literal `main` refuses (probe: read on both sides).
- Declared deviation 2, a continuation set wider than the claim's `+` and `.` example: correct in direction and correct JavaScript for every member but one pair. A next line opening with `(`, `[`, a backtick, `/`, `*`, `%`, `.`, `?`, `&`, `|`, `^`, `=`, a less-than or greater-than sign, or a binary `+` or `-` does continue the expression; JavaScript inserts no semicolon there. The exception is a next line opening with `++` or `--` (N1). A next line opening with `!`, `{`, `]`, `:`, a quote or an identifier is correctly not a continuation.
- Declared narrowing of the local gate set (2 NOT MEASURED): CI's to answer; `Build Core` and the test shards were pending at my read (above).
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff is two regular-expression fragments and prose; no query, no id materialisation, no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/data/hook-refusal-codes.ts`, against the card's ask, the docblock it cites and its two consumers.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- Property form, `(?=\s*[,}])`: holds. In valid JavaScript a property value that is one string literal can only be followed by whitespace, a comment, `,` or `}`; comments are blanked with their line breaks kept, and the terminator always lies inside the sliced `throw` statement (bracket depth above zero). `{ reason: 'x' }` items inside either `reasons` list close with `}` or `,`; the list's own `]` never follows a reason directly. `reasons: ['a', 'b']` was not read on `main` and is not read now. The only property shapes that go dark are computed (`'X' + s`, `'X' || y`, `'X' ? a : b`), an unparseable unclosed object, and `throw wrap(f ? code : 'X')`-style identifier misreads that end the statement, which were false reads.
- Assignment form: the lookahead is zero-width, the negated class excludes `\s` so `\s*` cannot backtrack into a false pass, and the flags carry no `m`, so `$` is the source end as the docblock says.
- N1 (nit) — three valid-JavaScript literals that `main` read and the head reads as computed (probe), against the sentence "as JavaScript reads it": (a) `e.code = 'X'` at a line end whose next line opens with `++` or `--` (JavaScript ends the statement there; a prefix update is not a continuation); (b) a ternary consequent on one line, `ok ? e.code = 'X' : e.code = 'Y'` (the `X` is lost, the `Y` kept; with `:` on the next line both are kept); (c) `[e.code = 'X']`. Also a bare CR line end and a no-break space before the line end. Each is a lost save refusal that the run-time refusal still answers, naming the code; none is a shape an author or the handler path's `toString` text plausibly produces. Accepted deviation; a follow-up could add `:` and `]` to the terminator set and exempt `++` and `--` from the continuation class.
- N2 (nit) — the reason pairing moves with a code that becomes computed (① above): a nested or reassigned computed code can make a reason newly read under the remaining literal code. For the nested shape the new save refusal is one the run also makes. For the reassigned shape it is the flow-insensitive pairing `main` already applies to `e.code = 'B'; e.code = compute(); e.reason = 'r'`, now also reached by a literal-prefixed value. No pin covers either. Accepted deviation; no change asked.
- N3 (nit) — a computed value still read as literal: a next line opening with the word operators `in` or `instanceof` (`e.code = 'X'` then `in obj`) continues the expression in JavaScript and is still read as the literal, as on `main`. The same-line spellings are dark. No other reverse case found: `'X' + s`, `'X'.concat(s)`, `'X' || y`, a continuation after blank or comment lines, and a template with a hole are all dark on both forms.
- N4 (nit, prose) — docblock of `ASSIGNMENT_VALUE_END`: "opens with an operator ... continues it, as JavaScript reads it" is loose both ways (`!` is an operator and does not continue; `++` and `--` do not continue in JavaScript and are treated as continuing). The other docblock hunks say what the code does, sentence by sentence.

Read, not reviewed (changeset, the lane seat's): its sentences on the two terminator sets, the worked examples and the run-time answer are true against the code. One is too wide: "Every literal code or reason the save refused before is still refused" is true of every shape it lists and false for the N1 shapes; "the ordinary literal forms" would be exact.
